paper.title: A Flux Map-Based Approach for Experimental Characterization of an Ipm 2-In-1 Drive Unit for Electric Vehicles
paper.level: Bibliographic source verified from release README, Dataverse related publication field, Crossref and OpenAlex; full paper not verified.

methods: Read numeric operating-point rows from FluxMap Test (row 120 headers) and Loss Test (row 140 headers); skip unit rows. Report each dq feedback minus its matched command and the vector norm in Apk. Loss Test speed bins use nearest 100 rpm; all rows also summarized by sheet. As a diagnostic fit unweighted least squares intercept+Iq and intercept+Iq+Id×Iq to FluxMap rows only, separately for D2_Torque_Feedback and tqDyno1Total. Score the same coefficients on Loss Test; report output-scale RMSE.
results: 142 flux-map rows near 1,003 rpm and 136 loss-test rows spanning 199–11,000 rpm. Vector tracking-error RMS 0.574 and 1.672 Apk, p95 1.129 and 4.077 Apk, respectively. On Loss Test, Iq-only RMSE 0.064 Nm on D2_Torque_Feedback; adding interaction yields 0.064 Nm. For tqDyno1Total it falls from 234.345 to 125.621 Nm. Results differ materially by output channel; preserve both published labels.
limits: The README calls D2_Torque_Feedback dyno torque feedback and tqDyno1Total gear-ratio-scaled dyno torque. The fit statistics are specific to the two released channels; the derivation does not assume a fixed conversion or independent torque transducers. The two sheets are from the same drive, have different speed/current coverage, and contain aggregated operating points. No high-rate actuating voltage command/applied pair, anti-windup state, clipping flag or transient reset is measured by these summaries.
reproduce: Fetch the original workbook at files[].download under its original name. Run python borealis-ipm.py RAW OUT. Python 3, NumPy 2.3.5, openpyxl 3.1.5.
evidence_level: Source files downloaded and parsed; derived summaries reproduced. Third-party source files are linked at the repository of record.
